transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, my mind just keeps going blank. At work. I'll be looking at the road-closure forms, or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and... I just can't remember what to do. Things I've done for years. It just... goes.
When your mind goes blank, are you aware of your surroundings, or do you lose track of time and find yourself in a different place or situation than you expected?
No... I know where I am. I don't end up anywhere else. I just... I'm just standing there, and I don't know what to do next. But I know I'm at work.
During these moments when your mind goes blank, do you ever notice any unusual body movements, like lip smacking, picking at your clothes, or muscle twitching?
No... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. I just... stand there.

Have you noticed any other changes in your memory or ability to handle daily tasks, such as managing your finances, cooking, or following complex instructions, outside of these moments where your mind goes blank?

I guess... yeah. I just haven't been reliable at work. I can't finish the paperwork, like I said, and... I don't trust myself with the traffic safety steps anymore. And outside of work... I just stopped doing things. I used to sing in a choir, and volunteer, but... I pulled away from all that. And my family. I just stayed away until... well, until they felt like they had to bring me here.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since you started feeling this way?

I don't really think about food much anymore. I guess I just... forget to eat. I don't really notice until I put on my work pants and they feel too big. My family... they've been asking why I look so thin, but... I just don't have an appetite. Sleep is... I don't know. Just normal, I guess.
Do you feel like your movements, speech, or thoughts have physically slowed down to the point where others might notice it?

I guess so... my family says I move like I'm underwater. It just takes me a really long time to... bathe, or get dressed. Even just getting to the door. But then... sometimes it's the opposite, and I can't settle at all. I just end up pacing the hallway... wringing my hands.
When you are pacing or feeling like you are moving through water, do you ever hear voices or see things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

Yes... sometimes. I... I hear things. When I'm home and it's quiet, or... even when I'm out near a work zone. I hear voices. They're... really clear. They call my name and... they tell me I've caused trouble on the block. But... no one else ever seems to hear them.

Looking back, did you feel like you were struggling with this deep sadness and lack of energy before you first started hearing those voices, or did the voices start at the same time as these other feelings?

No... it was before. Before the sadness got so deep. I was... I was still going to work and church for a few weeks, but I was already hearing my name. And... I don't really like talking about it, but... I started believing the street signs and the radios were sending messages about me. So, the voices and all that... they started first.

Looking at the entire time you have been feeling unwell, would you say that you have been experiencing these deep feelings of sadness and low energy for the majority of the time that you have been hearing these voices?

Yes... I suppose so. Most of the time, I've just felt... really heavy and sad. It's been like that for most of this... whole thing. Even when the voices aren't as loud, or I'm not thinking about the signs... the sadness is still there. It takes up most of it.
Can you recall any period of at least two weeks where you were hearing those voices or feeling like the signs were sending you messages, but you were not feeling that deep sadness or lack of energy?

Yes... I think I mentioned that. Before the... the heaviness really set in. There were a few weeks. I was still going to my post as a crossing guard, still going to church... but I was already hearing them. Hearing my name. And... noticing the signs and the radio. It was just that, for a little while, before the sadness took over.
